## Summary of Changes Hello @chrislusf, I'm Gemini Code Assist[^1]! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed! This pull request enhances the robustness of the WeedFS mount by introducing mechanisms to invalidate directory caches when the metadata subscription encounters errors and retries. This change prevents the display of stale directory listings to users after network interruptions or reconnections, ensuring that the file system mount accurately reflects the current state of the filer. ### Highlights * **Cache Invalidation Function**: A new function, `InvalidateAllChildrenCache`, has been added to the `InodeToPath` struct to clear the cached children status and expiration times for all directory entries, ensuring stale directory listings are removed. * **Metadata Subscription Retry Callback**: The `SubscribeMetaEvents` function now accepts an `onRetry` callback, which is executed whenever the metadata subscription encounters an error and attempts to reconnect or retry. * **Automatic Cache Cleanup on Retry**: The `weedfs` mount process has been updated to utilize the new `onRetry` callback. Upon a metadata subscription retry, it now explicitly clears the root folder's children from the meta cache and invalidates all children caches within `inodeToPath`. 🧠 **New Feature in Public Preview:** You can now enable **Memory** to help **Gemini Code Assist** learn from your team's feedback. This makes future code reviews more consistent and personalized to your project's style. **Click [here](https://codeassist.google/code-review/login) to enable Memory in your admin console.**
Using Gemini Code Assist
The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our [documentation page](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code), here are some quick tips. Invoking Gemini You can request assistance from Gemini at any point by creating a comment using either `/gemini ` or `@gemini-code-assist `. Below is a summary of the supported commands on the current page. Feature | Command | Description --- | --- | --- Code Review | `/gemini review` | Performs a code review for the current pull request in its current state. Pull Request Summary | `/gemini summary` | Provides a summary of the current pull request in its current state. Comment | @gemini-code-assist | Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in pull request comments and review comments. Help | `/gemini help` | Displays a list of available commands. Customization To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a `.gemini/` folder in the base of the repository. Detailed instructions can be found [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Limitations & Feedback Gemini Code Assist may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with :thumbsup: and :thumbsdown: on @gemini-code-assist comments. If you're interested in giving your feedback about your experience with Gemini Code Assist for Github and other Google products, sign up [here](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2cyuGuTWsEw84yG). You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the [Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/code-assist).
[^1]: Review the [Privacy Notices](https://policies.google.com/privacy), [Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy](https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy), [Terms of Service](https://policies.google.com/terms), and learn how to configure Gemini Code Assist in GitHub [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Gemini can make mistakes, so double check it and [use code with caution](https://support.google.com/legal/answer/13505487).

📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough Adds a bulk children-cache invalidation method to InodeToPath and wires an onRetry callback into meta-event subscription; the retry callback clears meta-cache root children and calls the new invalidation when subscription retries occur. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Inode-to-Path Cache**
`weed/mount/inode_to_path.go`|Added `InvalidateAllChildrenCache()` to lock the structure and clear `isChildrenCached` and `cachedExpiresTime` for all directory entries.| |**Meta Subscription**
`weed/mount/meta_cache/meta_cache_subscribe.go`|Updated `SubscribeMetaEvents()` signature to accept `onRetry func(lastTsNs int64, err error)` and invoke it on retry before logging.| |**Background Tasks Integration**
`weed/mount/weedfs.go`|`StartBackgroundTasks()` now supplies an `onRetry` callback that logs retries, deletes root meta-folder children from MetaCache, and calls `InvalidateAllChildrenCache()` on failures.| ## Sequence Diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant StartBG as StartBackgroundTasks() participant Subscribe as SubscribeMetaEvents() participant MetaStream as MetaEventStream participant onRetry as onRetry Callback participant MetaCache as MetaCache participant InodeToPath as InodeToPath StartBG->>Subscribe: subscribe(..., onRetry) Subscribe->>MetaStream: open stream / listen MetaStream-->>Subscribe: error / disconnect Subscribe->>onRetry: onRetry(lastTsNs, err) onRetry->>MetaCache: Delete root folder children onRetry->>InodeToPath: InvalidateAllChildrenCache() InodeToPath->>InodeToPath: clear isChildrenCached / reset cachedExpiresTime onRetry-->>Subscribe: callback complete Subscribe->>MetaStream: retry subscription MetaStream-->>Subscribe: events (on success) ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes ## Possibly related PRs - seaweedfs/seaweedfs#7818: Also changes mount cache handling and touches `weed/mount/weedfs.go` subscription logic. - seaweedfs/seaweedfs#7697: Makes changes to `inode_to_path.go` (related cache handling / nil-checks) and overlaps the same type. ## Poem > 🐇 I nibbled bytes beneath moon's light, > > Cleared the crumbs of cached delight. > > A retry hops, I tidy the trail, > > Fresh roots sprout where old bits fail. > > Hooray — the mount is neat and bright!

The required threshold is 80.00%. | Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold. | | Description check | ❓ Inconclusive | The description is incomplete. While it provides a summary of what the PR does, it lacks required sections like 'What problem are we solving?', 'How are we solving the problem?', and 'How is the PR tested?' from the template. The testing section only states 'not run (not requested)' without context. | Expand the description to follow the template: clearly explain the problem being solved, the solution approach, and provide more detail on testing strategy even if tests were not run. |
✅ Passed checks (1 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :---------: | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The title accurately summarizes the main change: invalidating the meta cache on follow retry, which directly reflects the code additions across all three modified files. |

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
